title.zh: 卷二十七 列傳第八 劉懷珍 李安民 王玄載
title.en: Volume 27 Biographies 8: Liu Huaizhen, Li Anmin, Wang Xuanzai
title.raw: 卷二十七 列傳第八 劉懷珍 李安民 王玄載 Volume 27 Biographies 8: Liu Huaizhen, Li Anmin, Wang Xuanzai

sentences.zh: 劉懷珍 李安民 王玄載

translations.literal: Liu Huaizhen, Li Anmin, Wang Xuanzai
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaizhen, Li Anmin, Wang Xuanzai

sentences.zh: 劉懷珍字道玉，平原人，漢膠東康王後也。

translations.literal: Liu Huaizhen, styled Daoyu, was a native of Pingyuan; he was a descendant of the Prince of Jiaodong of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaizhen, styled Daoyu, was a man of Pingyuan, descended from the Prince of Jiaodong of Han.

sentences.zh: 祖昶，宋武帝平齊，以為青州治中，至員外常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang, when Emperor Wu of Song pacified Qi, was made Qingzhou administrative officer and rose to supernumerary palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang, when Song's Emperor Wu conquered Qi, served as Qingzhou administrative officer and reached supernumerary palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 伯父奉伯，宋世為陳南頓二郡太守。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Fengbo served in the Song as prefect of Chen and Nandun.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Fengbo held the prefectures of Chen and Nandun under the Song.

sentences.zh: 懷珍幼隨奉伯至壽陽，豫州刺史趙伯符出獵，百姓聚觀，懷珍獨避不視，奉伯異之，曰：「此兒方興吾宗。」

translations.literal: As a boy Huaizhen followed Fengbo to Shouyang; when Yuzhou Inspector Zhao Bofu went hunting the people crowded to watch, but Huaizhen alone drew aside and would not look; Fengbo marveled and said: 「This boy will raise up our clan.」
translations.idiomatic: In boyhood Huaizhen went with Fengbo to Shouyang; when Inspector Zhao Bofu of Yuzhou went out hunting the common folk thronged to see, but Huaizhen alone stepped aside and would not look; Fengbo wondered at it and said: 「This child will lift up our house.」

sentences.zh: 本州辟主簿。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The province took him on as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十八年，亡命司馬順則聚黨東陽，州遣懷珍將數千人掩討平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia the outlaw Sima Shunze gathered a band in Dongyang; the province sent Huaizhen with several thousand men in a surprise attack and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year twenty-eight the outlaw Sima Shunze raised a following in Dongyang; the province sent Huaizhen with several thousand men to strike by surprise and bring him down.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝召問破賊事狀，懷珍讓功不肯當，親人怪問焉，懷珍曰：「昔國子尼恥陳河間之級，吾豈能論邦域之捷哉！

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song summoned him to ask about the defeat of the bandits; Huaizhen yielded the credit and would not accept it; kin wondered and asked him, and Huaizhen said: 「In old days Guo Zini was shamed by the rank of Hejian—how could I boast of victory within the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen summoned him to report on the rout of the band; Huaizhen declined the credit and would not take it; his kin marveled and asked why, and he said: 「Long ago Guo Zini was ashamed when Chen won the rank of Hejian—how could I trade on a triumph within the realm!

sentences.zh: 」時人稱之。

translations.literal: 」People praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: 」Men praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭出鎮盱眙，道遇懷珍，以應對見重，取為驃騎長兼墨曹行參軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong went out to command at Xuyi he met Huaizhen on the road; impressed by his answers, he took him as chief secretary concurrently acting Secretariat clerk on the Rapid Cavalry staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jiangxia Yigong marched out to Xuyi he met Huaizhen on the road; struck by his replies, he made him chief secretary and acting secretariat clerk on the rapid-cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 尋除振武將軍、長廣太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General of Shaking Arms and prefect of Changgang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named general of shaking arms and prefect of Changgang.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，為義恭大司馬參軍、直閤將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he served Yigong as Grand Marshal staff officer and colonel of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Xiaojian he was staff officer on Yigong's grand-marshal staff and colonel of the direct gate.

sentences.zh: 懷珍北州舊姓，門附殷積，啟上門生千人充宿衛。

translations.literal: Huaizhen was an old-name family of the northern provinces with many dependents; he memorialized that a thousand of his house students be enrolled in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen came of an old northern house with a great following; he asked that a thousand of his private students fill the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 孝武大驚，召取青、冀豪家私附得數千人，士人怨之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was greatly alarmed and summoned the great households of Qing and Ji who had private attachments—several thousand in all; the gentry resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was alarmed and called up the great clans of Qing and Ji with private retinues—several thousand men—and the gentry bitterly resented it.

sentences.zh: 隨府轉太宰參軍。

translations.literal: He followed the headquarters to transfer as Grand Heir staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the command post and was moved to staff officer of the grand heir.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，虜圍泗口城，青州刺史顏師伯請援。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming the barbarians besieged Sikou city; Qingzhou Inspector Yan Shibo asked for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming year two the northerners besieged Sikou; Yan Shibo, inspector of Qingzhou, begged for aid.

sentences.zh: 孝武遣懷珍將步騎數千赴之，於麋溝湖與虜戰羣，破七城。

translations.literal: Xiaowu sent Huaizhen with several thousand foot and horse to go; at Miyugou Lake they fought the barbarians in a swarm and broke seven cities.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu sent Huaizhen with several thousand foot and horse; at Miyugou Lake they met the enemy host and took seven towns.

sentences.zh: 拜建武將軍、樂陵河間二郡太守，賜爵廣晉縣侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Martial Might and prefect of Leiling and Hejian, enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangjin.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who establishes martial might and prefect of Leiling and Hejian, and enfeoffed as marquis of Guangjin.

sentences.zh: 明年，懷珍啟求還，孝武答曰：「邊維須才，未宜陳請。

translations.literal: The next year Huaizhen memorialized asking to return; Xiaowu answered: 「The frontier still needs talent—you should not yet plead to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Huaizhen asked to go home; Xiaowu replied: 「The borderlands still want your kind—this is no time to ask leave.

sentences.zh: 」竟陵王誕反，郡豪民王弼勸懷珍應之，懷珍斬弼以聞。

translations.literal: 」The Prince of Jingling Dan rebelled; a leading man of the district Wang Bi urged Huaizhen to join him; Huaizhen beheaded Bi and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: 」When Prince of Jingling Dan rose, a local magnate Wang Bi pressed Huaizhen to follow him; Huaizhen cut off Bi's head and sent word up.

sentences.zh: 孝武大喜，除豫章王子尚車騎參軍，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Xiaowu was greatly pleased and made him chariot staff officer to Prince Zishang of Yuzhang, with additional title General of the Flying Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu was delighted and made him chariot staff officer to Prince Zishang of Yuzhang, with the added rank of general of the flying dragon.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，除寧朔將軍、東安東莞二郡太守，率龍驤將軍王敬則、姜產步騎五千討壽陽。

translations.literal: At the start of Taishi he was made General of Pacifying the North and prefect of Dong'an and Dongguan, leading the Flying Dragon General Wang Jingze and Jiang Chan with five thousand foot and horse to attack Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taishi he was named general of pacifying the north and prefect of Dong'an and Dongguan, and marched with Wang Jingze, general of the flying dragon, and Jiang Chan at five thousand foot and horse against Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守王仲子南奔，賊遣偽廬江太守劉道蔚五千人頓建武澗，築三城。

translations.literal: Lujiang Prefect Wang Zhongzi fled south; the rebels sent a false Lujiang prefect Liu Daowei with five thousand men to hold Jianwujian and raise three forts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongzi, prefect of Lujiang, fled south; the rebels set a false prefect Liu Daowei with five thousand men at Jianwujian and built three walled camps.

sentences.zh: 懷珍遣軍主段僧愛等馬步三百餘人掩擊斬之。

translations.literal: Huaizhen sent the army commander Duan Song'ai and others, horse and foot three hundred odd, in a surprise strike—they beheaded Daowei.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen sent his commander Duan Song'ai and others—three hundred odd horse and foot—in a night strike and took Daowei's head.

sentences.zh: 引軍至晉熙，偽太守閻湛拒守，劉子勛遣將王仲虯步卒萬人救之，懷珍遣馬步三千人襲擊仲虯，大破之於莫邪山，遂進壽陽。

translations.literal: He led the army to Jinxi; the false prefect Yan Zhan held firm; Liu Zixun sent the general Wang Zhongjiao with ten thousand foot soldiers to relieve him; Huaizhen sent three thousand horse and foot to strike Zhongjiao, routed him utterly at Moye Mountain, and pressed on to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Jinxi, where the false prefect Yan Zhan held the walls; Liu Zixun sent Wang Zhongjiao with ten thousand foot to relieve him; Huaizhen sent three thousand horse and foot against Zhongjiao, broke him on Moye Mountain, and pushed on to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 又遣王敬則破殷琰將劉從等四壘於橫塘死虎，懷珍等乘勝逐北，頓壽春長邏門。

translations.literal: He also sent Wang Jingze to break four camps of Yin Yan's general Liu Cong and others at Hengtang Dead Tiger; Huaizhen and the rest rode the victory in pursuit north to camp at the Changluo Gate of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Jingze to smash four camps of Yin Yan's Liu Cong and the rest at Dead Tiger on Hengtang; Huaizhen and his men rode the rout north and halted at the long patrol gate of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝嘉其功，除羽林監、屯騎校尉，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song rewarded his merit and made him Inspector of the Feathered Forest and colonel of the dismounted cavalry, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song honored his service and made him inspector of the feathered forest and colonel of the dismounted cavalry, with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 懷珍請先平賊，辭讓不受。

translations.literal: Huaizhen asked first to finish the rebels and declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen begged to end the rebels first and would not take the post.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁濃湖與賊相持，久未決。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren at Nonghu held the rebels at stalemate, long undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren at Thick Lake faced the rebels in a long standoff with no end.

sentences.zh: 明帝召懷珍還，拜前將軍，加輔國將軍，領軍向青山助擊劉胡，事平，除游擊將軍，輔國將軍如故。

translations.literal: Ming summoned Huaizhen back, made him former general with additional Fuguo general, led the army toward Qingshan to help strike Liu Hu; when the affair was settled he was made General of the Roaming Attack, fuguo general as before.
translations.idiomatic: Ming called Huaizhen back, made him former general with added rank of fuguo general, and sent him with the host toward Green Mountain to help crush Liu Hu; when peace came he was named general of the roaming attack, fuguo general as before.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史沈文秀拒命，明帝遣其弟文炳宣喻，使懷珍領馬步三千人隨文炳俱行。

translations.literal: Qingzhou Inspector Shen Wenxiu defied orders; Ming sent his younger brother Wenbing to announce and persuade, and had Huaizhen lead three thousand horse and foot to go with Wenbing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenxiu, inspector of Qingzhou, refused obedience; Ming sent his brother Wenbing to proclaim the throne's will and ordered Huaizhen with three thousand horse and foot to go with him.

sentences.zh: 未至，薛安都引虜，徐、兖已沒，張永、沈攸之於彭城大敗。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Xue Andu brought in the barbarians; Xu and Yan were lost; Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi suffered great defeat at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before they came up, Xue Andu called in the northerners; Xu and Yan fell; Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi were routed at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 勑懷珍步從盱眙自淮陰濟淮救永等，而官軍為虜所逐，相繼奔歸，懷珍乃還。

translations.literal: They ordered Huaizhen on foot to follow from Xuyi, cross the Huai from Huaiyin to save Yong and the rest, but the government army was driven by the barbarians and fled back in succession, and Huaizhen returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was told to march on foot from Xuyi, cross the Huai at Huaiyin, and rescue Yong and the others, but the imperial columns were harried by the enemy and broke back one after another, and Huaizhen turned home.

sentences.zh: 三年春，敕懷珍權鎮山陽。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year he was ordered to hold Shanyang in acting authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, spring, he was ordered to govern Shanyang in acting charge.

sentences.zh: 先是明帝遣青州刺史明僧暠北征，僧暠遣將於王城築壘，以逼沈文秀，壍壁未立，為文秀所破，仍進攻僧暠。

translations.literal: Earlier Ming had sent Qingzhou Inspector Ming Sengchao on the northern expedition; Sengchao sent generals to build forts at Wangcheng to press Shen Wenxiu—the ramparts were not yet done when Wenxiu broke them and pressed the attack on Sengchao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ming had sent Ming Sengchao of Qingzhou on the northern campaign; Sengchao sent officers to raise forts at Wangcheng against Shen Wenxiu—the walls were not yet finished when Wenxiu overran them and drove on Sengchao.

sentences.zh: 帝使懷珍率龍驤將軍王廣之五百騎，步卒二千人，沿海救援，至東海，而僧暠已退保東萊。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Huaizhen with Flying Dragon General Wang Guangzhi, five hundred horse and two thousand foot, along the coast to relieve them; they reached Donghai, but Sengchao had already withdrawn to hold Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent Huaizhen with Wang Guangzhi, general of the flying dragon, at five hundred horse and two thousand foot along the coast to relieve him; they came to Donghai, but Sengchao had already pulled back to defend Donglai.

sentences.zh: 懷珍進據朐城，衆心忷懼，或欲且保郁州。

translations.literal: Huaizhen advanced to hold Qucheng; the host was fearful and some wished for the time to hold Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen moved up and seized Qucheng; hearts wavered, and some urged a pause at Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷珍謂衆曰：「卿等傳文秀厚賂胡師，規為外援，察其徒黨，何能必就左衽。

translations.literal: Huaizhen told the host: 「You keep saying Wenxiu has bribed the Hu chieftains heavily and means to summon outside aid—but look at his following: can they truly all turn barbarian?
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen told the men: 「You say Wenxiu has heaped bribes on the Hu generals and plots outside help—but look at the men at his side: will they all truly go over to the left-hand dress?

sentences.zh: 齊士庶見於名義積葉，聲介一馳，東萊可飛書而下，何容阻軍緩邁止於此邪？

translations.literal: The gentlemen and commoners of Qi have seen honor and shame piled for generations; let one report fly ahead and Donglai will surrender by letter—how can you hold the army here and dawdle?
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and common folk of Qi have watched honor and shame gather for generations; let one call run ahead and Donglai will fall to a dispatch—how can we choke the army here and crawl along?

sentences.zh: 」遂進至黔陬。

translations.literal: 」He advanced to Qianqu.
translations.idiomatic: 」He pushed on to Qianqu.

sentences.zh: 偽高密、平昌二郡太守潰走，懷珍達朝廷意，送致文炳，文秀終不從命，焚燒郭邑。

translations.literal: The false prefects of Gaomi and Pingchang fled; Huaizhen conveyed the court's intent and forwarded Wenbing; Wenxiu still would not obey and burned the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel prefects of Gaomi and Pingchang broke and ran; Huaizhen carried the court's word and sent Wenbing forward; Wenxiu still refused and burned the outer town.

sentences.zh: 百姓聞懷珍至，皆喜。

translations.literal: When the people heard Huaizhen had come, they were all glad.
translations.idiomatic: When the people heard Huaizhen was near, they rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 偽長廣太守劉桃根領數

translations.literal: The false Governor of Changguang Liu Taogen led several
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taogen, the rebel governor of Changguang, led several

translations.literal: ten
translations.idiomatic: ten

sentences.zh: ［千］人戍不其城，懷珍引軍次洋水。

translations.literal: thousand men garrisoning Buqi city; Huaizhen led the army to camp at Yangshui.
translations.idiomatic: thousand men to hold Buqi; Huaizhen brought the host to encamp on the Yangshui.

sentences.zh: 衆皆曰：「文秀今游騎滿境內，宜堅壁伺隙。

translations.literal: All said: 「Wenxiu now has light horse all through the land—you should hold the walls and watch for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: The men all said: 「Wenxiu's scouts now fill the country—you should shut the gates and wait for a gap.

sentences.zh: 」懷珍曰：「今衆少糧單，我懸彼固，政宜簡精銳，掩其不備耳。

translations.literal: 」Huaizhen said: 「We are few and grain thin, we hang before their strength—that is exactly when to pick elites and catch them unready.
translations.idiomatic: 」Huaizhen said: 「We are few and grain light, hung out before their walls—that is when to choose the keenest and strike before they know it.

sentences.zh: 」遣王廣之將百騎襲陷其城，桃根走。

translations.literal: 」He sent Wang Guangzhi with a hundred horse in a surprise raid and took the city; Taogen fled.
translations.idiomatic: 」He sent Wang Guangzhi with a hundred horse in a night rush and seized the town; Taogen ran.

sentences.zh: 偽東萊太守鞠延僧數百人據城，劫留高麗獻使。

translations.literal: The false Donglai prefect Ju Yanseng with several hundred men held the city and detained the Korea tribute envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Yanseng, the false prefect of Donglai, with several hundred men held the city and held up the Korean tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 懷珍又遣寧朔將軍明慶符與廣之擊降延僧，遣高麗使詣京師。

translations.literal: Huaizhen again sent Pacifying North General Ming Qingfu with Guangzhi to strike and make Yanseng yield, and sent the Korean envoy to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen again sent Ming Qingfu, general of pacifying the north, with Guangzhi to beat Yanseng into surrender and sent the Korean envoys to the capital.

sentences.zh: 文秀聞諸城皆敗，乃遣使張靈碩請降，懷珍乃還。

translations.literal: When Wen Xiu heard that every city had fallen, he sent his envoy Zhang Lingshuo to offer surrender, and Huaizhen then returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Xiu learned that every stronghold had fallen, he sent Zhang Lingshuo to sue for surrender, and Huaizhen withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其秋，虜遂侵齊，圍歷城、梁鄒二城，游騎至東陽，擾動百姓。

translations.literal: That autumn the northerners invaded Qi, besieged the two cities Licheng and Liangzou, and raiding horsemen reached Dongyang and stirred the people.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the enemy swept into Qi, laid siege to Licheng and Liangzou, and scouting horsemen reached Dongyang and threw the countryside into alarm.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史崔道固、兖州刺史劉休賓告急。

translations.literal: Ji Province Inspector Cui Daogu and Yan Province Inspector Liu Xiubin sent urgent appeals.
translations.idiomatic: Ji inspector Cui Daogu and Yan inspector Liu Xiubin cried for help.

sentences.zh: 休賓，懷珍從弟也。

translations.literal: Xiubin was Huaizhen's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin was Huaizhen's cousin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以懷珍為使持節、都督徐兖二州軍事、輔國將軍、平胡中郎將、徐州刺史，封艾縣侯，邑四百戶，督水步四十餘軍赴救。

translations.literal: The court made Huaizhen Bearer of the Staff, overseer of military affairs in Xu and Yan, General Who Assists the State, General Who Pacifies the Hu as central commandant, and Governor of Xu; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Ai with a fief of four hundred households and led more than forty armies by land and water to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Huaizhen bearer of the staff, overseer of Xu and Yan, general who assists the state, general who pacifies the Hu as central commandant, and governor of Xu, enfeoffed him Marquis of Ai at four hundred households, and sent him with more than forty land and river armies to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 二城旣沒，乃止。

translations.literal: Both cities had already fallen, so he halted.
translations.idiomatic: Both cities were already lost, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 改授寧朔將軍、竟陵太守，轉巴陵王征西司馬，領南義陽太守。

translations.literal: He was reassigned General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Jingling, then made western campaign staff officer to the Prince of Baling while holding Administrator of Southern Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the north and administrator of Jingling, then staff officer on the Prince of Baling's western campaign while holding southern Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素為荊州，仍徙右軍司馬，遷南郡太守，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jianping, Jing Su, went to Jingzhou, Huaizhen was moved to right army staff officer, then Administrator of Nan commandery with the added rank of General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jianping Jing Su took Jingzhou, Huaizhen was shifted to right army staff officer, then administrator of Nan commandery with general who pacifies the north added to his title.

sentences.zh: 明帝手詔懷珍曰：「卿性忠讜，平所仗賴。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming wrote Huaizhen by hand: 「Your nature is loyal and outspoken; in peace I have leaned on you.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming wrote to Huaizhen in his own hand: 「You are loyal and plain-spoken; in quiet times I have trusted you.

sentences.zh: 在彼與年少共事，不可深存受益。

translations.literal: There you serve with a young man; do not seek deep private gain.
translations.idiomatic: There you work beside a youth; do not hoard profit for yourself.

sentences.zh: 景素兒乃佳，但不能接物，頗亦墮事，卿每諫之。

translations.literal: Jing Su's son is fine, but he cannot meet people halfway and has rather fallen into neglect; you must counsel him each time.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Su's boy has merit, yet he cannot handle men and has let affairs slide; admonish him whenever you can.

sentences.zh: 」懷珍奉旨。

translations.literal: 」Huaizhen obeyed the command.
translations.idiomatic: 」Huaizhen took the edict to heart.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，又詔懷珍曰：「卿不應乃作景素佐，才舊所寄，今徵卿參二衛直。

translations.literal: When the emperor lay ill he again addressed Huaizhen: 「You ought not to be Jing Su's aide; your talent is an old trust of mine. Now I summon you to direct service in the two guards.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor grew grave he wrote again: 「You should not serve as Jing Su's lieutenant; your talent has long been in my keeping. I now call you to the two guards on direct duty.

sentences.zh: 」會帝崩，乃為安成王撫軍司馬，領南高平太守。

translations.literal: 」But the emperor died; Huaizhen was then made pacification army staff officer to the Prince of Ancheng and held Administrator of Southern Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: 」Before the summons could take, the emperor died. Huaizhen became pacification army staff officer to the Prince of Ancheng and administrator of southern Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑桂陽王休範，中書舍人王道隆宣旨，以懷珍為冠軍將軍、豫章太守。

translations.literal: The court suspected the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan; Palace Attendant Wang Daolong announced the will and made Huaizhen General Who Exerts Might and Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The court distrusted Prince of Guiyang Xiu Fan. Palace attendant Wang Daolong read the command and named Huaizhen general who exerts might and administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 懷珍曰：「休範須有禍萌，安敢便發，若終為寇，必請奉律吞之。

translations.literal: Huaizhen said: 「Xiu Fan must still show the bud of disaster; how dare he rise at once? If in the end he becomes a rebel, I shall ask leave to swallow him by the law.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen said: 「Xiu Fan has not yet shown the seed of treason; he will not dare move so soon. Should he turn rebel in the end, I shall beg to destroy him within the law.

sentences.zh: 今者賜使，恐成猜迫。

translations.literal: This present gift of an envoy may breed suspicion and pressure.
translations.idiomatic: This envoy sent to me now will only breed mistrust and haste.

sentences.zh: 」固請不就，乃除黃門郎，領虎賁中郎將、青州大中正。

translations.literal: 」He firmly begged not to take the post and was instead made Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, holding Tiger-Fang central commandant and chief evaluator of Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: 」He pressed his refusal until the court made him gentleman of the yellow gates, with tiger-fang central commandant and chief evaluator of Qing added.

sentences.zh: 桂陽反，加懷珍前將軍，守石頭。

translations.literal: When Guiyang rebelled, Huaizhen was advanced to General of the Van and guarded Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: When Guiyang rose, Huaizhen was made van general and held Shitou.

sentences.zh: 為使持節、督豫司二州郢州之西陽軍事、冠軍將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff, overseer of military affairs in Yu and Si and Xiyang in Ying, General Who Exerts Might, and Governor of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was bearer of the staff, overseer of Yu and Si and of Xiyang in Ying, general who exerts might, and governor of Yu.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素反，懷珍遣子靈哲領兵赴京師。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jianping, Jing Su, rebelled, Huaizhen sent his son Ling Zhe to lead troops to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jianping Jing Su rebelled, Huaizhen sent his son Ling Zhe with troops to the capital.

sentences.zh: 昇明元年，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming his title was advanced to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 1 he was raised to general who subdues the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之在荊楚，朝議疑惑，懷珍遣冗從僕射張護使郢，致誠於世祖，幷陳計策。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi held Jing and Chu; court opinion wavered. Huaizhen sent Supernumerary Master of Attendance Zhang Hu as envoy to Ying to pledge loyalty to Shizu and lay out his plans.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi held Jing and Chu and the court could not read him. Huaizhen sent supernumerary master of attendance Zhang Hu to Ying to swear loyalty to Shizu and set out his strategy.

sentences.zh: 及攸之起兵，衆謂當沿流直下，懷珍謂僚佐曰：「攸之矜躁夙著，虐加楚服，必當阻兵中流，聲劫幼主。

translations.literal: When Youzhi raised arms, many said he would drive straight downriver. Huaizhen told his staff: 「Youzhi's arrogance and rashness have long been known; he has heaped cruelty on the Chu lands. He is sure to block the river with arms and make a show of seizing the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi took the field, most expected him to sweep down the river. Huaizhen told his aides: 「Youzhi's pride and haste are old news, and his cruelty has worn out Chu. He will surely hold the midstream with troops and threaten the child emperor for show.

sentences.zh: 不敢長驅決勝明矣。

translations.literal: That he dares not drive far for a clean victory is plain.
translations.idiomatic: He will not dare a long march to decide the war—that much is clear.

sentences.zh: 」遣子靈哲領馬步數千人衛京師。

translations.literal: 」He sent his son Ling Zhe to lead several thousand horse and foot to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 」He sent Ling Zhe with several thousand horse and foot to shield the capital.

sentences.zh: 攸之遣使許天保說結懷珍，懷珍斬之，送首于太祖。

translations.literal: Youzhi sent his envoy Xu Tianbao to win Huaizhen over; Huaizhen beheaded him and sent the head to the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi sent Xu Tianbao to court him; Huaizhen struck off his head and forwarded it to the Founder.

sentences.zh: 太祖送示攸之。

translations.literal: The Founder sent it on for Youzhi to see.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder had it shown to Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 進號左將軍，徙封中宿縣侯，增邑六百戶。

translations.literal: Huaizhen's title was advanced to General of the Left; his fief was moved to Marquis of Zhongsu with six hundred households added.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to general of the left, his marquisate shifted to Zhongsu, and his fief increased by six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 攸之圍郢城，懷珍遣建寧太守張謨、游擊將軍裴仲穆統蠻漢軍萬人出西陽，破賊前鋒公孫方平軍數千人，收其器甲。

translations.literal: Youzhi besieged Ying city. Huaizhen sent Jianning Administrator Zhang Mo and Mobile Campaign General Pei Zhongmu to command ten thousand barbarian and Han troops out of Xiyang; they broke the rebel vanguard Gongsun Fangping's army of several thousand and seized weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi laid siege to Ying. Huaizhen sent Zhang Mo, administrator of Jianning, and Pei Zhongmu, mobile campaign general, with ten thousand mixed troops from Xiyang; they shattered several thousand of the rebel van under Gongsun Fangping and took arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 進平南將軍，增督南豫、北徐二州，增邑為千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, given added oversight of Southern Yu and Northern Xu, and his fief was raised to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the south, given added command of southern Yu and northern Xu, and his fief set at one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 初，孝武世，太祖為舍人，懷珍為直閤，相遇早舊。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the Founder was a palace gentleman and Huaizhen a direct-gate general; they had met as old companions.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, under Emperor Xiaowu, the Founder had been a palace gentleman and Huaizhen a direct-gate general, and they were already old friends.

sentences.zh: 懷珍假還青州，上有白驄馬，齧人，不可騎，送與懷珍別。

translations.literal: When Huaizhen took leave to return to Qing province, the throne had a white piebald horse that bit men and could not be ridden; it was sent to Huaizhen as a parting gift.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaizhen went home on leave to Qing, the court owned a white piebald that bit and could not be ridden; it was sent to him for farewell.

sentences.zh: 懷珍報上百匹絹。

translations.literal: Huaizhen sent back a hundred bolts of silk in return.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen returned a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 或謂懷珍曰：「蕭君此馬不中騎，是以與君耳。

translations.literal: Someone said to Huaizhen: 「Lord Xiao's horse was unfit to ride, and that is why he gave it to you.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Huaizhen: 「Lord Xiao's horse would not carry a man—that is why he gave it to you.

sentences.zh: 君報百匹，不亦多乎？

translations.literal: Yet you sent back a hundred bolts—is that not too much?
translations.idiomatic: A hundred bolts in return—is that not excessive?

sentences.zh: 」懷珍曰：「蕭君局量堂堂，寧應負人此絹。

translations.literal: 」Huaizhen said: 「Lord Xiao's measure is broad and high; surely he would not begrudge me this silk.
translations.idiomatic: 」Huaizhen said: 「Lord Xiao's breadth of mind is grand; he would not stint me this silk.

sentences.zh: 吾方欲以身名托之，豈計錢物多少。」

translations.literal: I mean to entrust him with my person and name—why should I reckon coin and goods?
translations.idiomatic: I am about to stake my person and reputation on him—why count cash and goods?

sentences.zh: 虜寇淮、肥，以本官加平西將軍，假節，西屯巢湖，為壽春勢援，虜退乃還。

translations.literal: When the enemy raided the Huai and Fei, he was given his existing rank plus General Who Pacifies the West with delegated staff, camped west at Chaohu as a buttress for Shouchun, and returned only after the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the northerners struck the Huai and Fei, he kept his present rank and added general who pacifies the west with delegated staff, camped west at Chaohu to shore up Shouchun, and came back once they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 懷珍年老，以禁旅辛勤，求為閒職，轉光祿大夫，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Huaizhen was old; finding palace guard duty wearisome, he asked for a lighter post and was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, his regular attendant rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In his years Huaizhen found palace guard service a grind and sought an easier office; he was made grand master for splendid happiness, still regular attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 其冬，虜寇朐山，授使持節、安北將軍，本官如故，領兵救授。

translations.literal: That winter, when the enemy raided Qushan, he was given Bearer of the Staff and General Who Pacifies the North, his former rank unchanged, and ordered to lead troops to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the enemy hit Qushan; he was bearer of the staff and general who pacifies the north at his old rank, and sent with troops to rescue.

sentences.zh: 未至，事寧，解安北、持節。

translations.literal: Before he arrived the affair was settled; he was relieved of Pacifies the North and the staff.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet arrived when the crisis ended; pacifies the north and the staff were taken back.

sentences.zh: 四年，疾篤，上表解職，上優詔答許，別量所授。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his illness grew grave; he memorialized to resign, and the throne answered with a gracious edict granting his request and setting his honors apart.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his sickness deepened; he asked to leave office, and the throne answered with a gracious edict, granting release and fixing his rewards apart.

sentences.zh: 其夏，卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: That summer he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 遺言薄葬。

translations.literal: His last words called for a plain burial.
translations.idiomatic: He left word for a spare funeral.

sentences.zh: 世祖追贈散騎常侍、鎮北將軍、雍州刺史，諡曰敬侯。

translations.literal: Shizu posthumously made him Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Yong, with the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu posthumously named him regular attendant of the scattered riders, general who pacifies the north, and governor of Yong, with the posthumous style Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子靈哲，字文明。

translations.literal: His son Ling Zhe, styled Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ling Zhe, styled Wenming.

sentences.zh: 解褐王國常侍、行參軍，尚書直郎，齊臺步兵校尉。

translations.literal: On first appointment he was kingdom regular attendant and acting staff officer, Inner Court direct gentleman, and infantry commandant of the Qi headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At his first posting he was kingdom regular attendant and acting staff officer, inner court direct gentleman, and infantry commandant on the Qi staff.

sentences.zh: 建元初，歷寧朔將軍，臨川王前軍諮議，廬陵內史，齊郡太守，前軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the opening of Jianyuan he served in turn as General Who Pacifies the North, front army adviser to the Prince of Linchuan, interior minister of Luling, administrator of Qi commandery, and General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianyuan opened he rose through general who pacifies the north, front army adviser to the Prince of Linchuan, interior minister of Luling, administrator of Qi commandery, and van general.

sentences.zh: 靈哲所生母嘗病，靈哲躬自祈禱，夢見黃衣老公曰：「可取南山竹笋食之，疾立可愈。

translations.literal: When Ling Zhe's birth mother fell ill, Ling Zhe prayed in person and dreamed of an old man in yellow robes who said: 「Take bamboo shoots from South Mountain and eat them; the illness will heal at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Ling Zhe's birth mother grew ill, he prayed himself and dreamed of an old man in yellow who said: 「Fetch bamboo shoots from South Mountain and eat them; the sickness will pass at once.

sentences.zh: 」靈哲驚覺，如言而疾瘳。

translations.literal: 」Ling Zhe woke in alarm; he did as told and the illness was quickly cured.
translations.idiomatic: 」Ling Zhe started awake; he did exactly as he had been told, and the sickness lifted at once.

sentences.zh: 嫡母崔氏及兄子景煥，泰始中沒虜，靈哲為布衣，不聽樂。

translations.literal: His stepmother, Lady Cui, and his elder brother's son Jinghuan were taken by the northerners in the Taishi era; Ling Zhe, still a commoner, would not listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi years his stepmother Lady Cui and his brother's son Jinghuan fell into northern hands; Ling Zhe, living as a private man, would not hear music played.

sentences.zh: 及懷珍卒，當襲爵，靈哲固辭以兄子在虜中，存亡未測，無容越當茅土，朝廷義之。

translations.literal: When Huaizhen died, the succession fell to him; Ling Zhe firmly declined, saying his brother's son was in barbarian lands and whether he lived or died could not be known—he could not step over him for a fief of earth. The court honored his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: At Huaizhen's death the title should have passed to him; Ling Zhe refused outright. His nephew was still among the northerners, his fate unknown—he would not leap over him to take a noble fief. The throne praised his sense of right.

sentences.zh: 靈哲傾產私贖嫡母及景煥，累年不能得。

translations.literal: Ling Zhe spent his whole fortune trying to ransom his stepmother and Jinghuan in secret; year after year he could not obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Zhe poured out his wealth to buy back his stepmother and Jinghuan on his own; years went by and he still could not bring them home.

sentences.zh: 世祖哀之，令北使告虜主，虜主送以還南，襲懷珍封爵。

translations.literal: Shizu pitied him and ordered the northern envoy to inform the barbarian ruler; the barbarian ruler sent them back south, and Ling Zhe inherited Huaizhen's enfeoffment and title.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu took pity and told the envoy to the north to speak with the barbarian king; the king sent them south again, and Ling Zhe at last entered upon Huaizhen's rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 靈哲永明初歷護軍長史，東中郎諮議，領中直兵，出為寧朔將軍、巴西梓潼二郡太守，西陽王左軍司馬。

translations.literal: In early Yongming, Ling Zhe served in turn as chief clerk of the Protector Army, consultative officer of the Eastern Central Commandant, and commander of the central guard troops; he went out as General Who Pacifies the North, administrator of the two commanderies Baxi and Zitong, and left-army chief clerk to the Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yongming, Ling Zhe rose through chief clerk of the Protector Army, consultative officer to the Eastern Central Commandant, and command of the central guard; he was then sent out as General Who Pacifies the North, governor of Baxi and Zitong, and left-army chief clerk to the Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang 1 he died, at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 李安民，蘭陵承人也。

translations.literal: Li Anmin was a man of Chen in Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Anmin came from Chen in Lanling commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖嶷，衛軍參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yao was a staff officer in the Army of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yao had served as a staff officer in the Army of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 父欽之，殿中將軍，補薛令。

translations.literal: His father Qin-zhi was a palace guard general and was appointed magistrate of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qin-zhi was a general of the palace guard and took up the magistracy of Xue.

sentences.zh: 安民隨父之縣，元嘉二十七年沒虜，率部曲自拔南歸。

translations.literal: Anmin followed his father to the county; in the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he was taken by the northerners, then led his retainers in breaking out and returning south.
translations.idiomatic: He went with his father to the county seat; in Yuanjia 27 he was captured by the northerners, but rallied his household troops and fought his way back south.

sentences.zh: 太初逆，使安民領支軍。

translations.literal: When the Taichu usurper turned traitor, Anmin was put in command of a detached force.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taichu rebellion he was ordered to lead a separate column.

sentences.zh: 降義師，板建威將軍，補魯爽左軍。

translations.literal: He surrendered to the righteous army and was appointed General Who Establishes Might, with a supplemental post on Lu Shuang's left wing.
translations.idiomatic: He came over to the loyal armies and was made General Who Establishes Might, with a supplemental appointment on Lu Shuang's left wing.

sentences.zh: 及爽反，安民遁還京師，除領軍行參軍，遷左衛殿中將軍。

translations.literal: When Shuang rebelled, Anmin slipped back to the capital; he was made acting officer on the staff of the Army of the Guard and promoted to palace guard of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang rose in revolt, Anmin stole back to the capital, became an acting staff officer of the Army of the Guard, and was raised to palace guard of the Left.

sentences.zh: 大明中，虜侵徐、兖，以安民為建威府司馬、無鹽令，除殿中將軍，領軍討漢川互螫賊。

translations.literal: In the Daming era the barbarians raided Xu and Yan; Anmin was made chief clerk of the Establishes Might headquarters and magistrate of Wuyan, then palace guard general, and led an army to suppress the bandits who were tearing each other apart in the Han River country.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daming, when the northerners pressed Xu and Yan, Anmin was named chief clerk of the Establishes Might headquarters and magistrate of Wuyan, then made a palace guard general and sent to crush the warring bandits of the Han River valleys.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勛反，明帝除安民武衛將軍、領水軍，補建安王司徒城局參軍，擊赭圻湖、白荻浦、獺窟，皆捷，除積射將軍、軍主。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun, rebelled, Mingdi made Anmin Martial Guard General and commander of the naval forces, with a supplemental post as staff officer of the city bureau under the Prince of Jian'an the Minister; he attacked Zheqi Lake, White Dike Ford, and Otter Den and carried every fight; he was made Volley General and army commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an rebelled, Mingdi named Anmin Martial Guard General, put the fleet in his hands, and added him as a city-bureau staff officer under the Prince of Jian'an; he stormed Zheqi Lake, White Dike Ford, and Otter Den to victory after victory, and was raised to Volley General and army commander.

sentences.zh: 張興世據錢溪，糧盡，為賊所逼。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi held Qianxi, but his grain was spent and the rebels had him pinned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingshi held Qianxi until his grain ran out and the enemy had him boxed in.

sentences.zh: 安民率舟乘數百，越賊五城，送米與興世。

translations.literal: Anmin led several hundred boats, passed over five rebel strongholds, and delivered rice to Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin took several hundred boats, slipped past five rebel camps, and ran grain through to Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 偽軍主沈仲、王張引軍自<魚貴>口欲斷江，安民進軍合戰破之。

translations.literal: The false army commanders Shen Zhong and Wang Zhang led troops from the Yugui crossing to cut the river; Anmin advanced, joined battle, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The puppet commanders Shen Zhong and Wang Zhang marched from the Yugui ford to sever the river line; Anmin moved up, met them in battle, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 又擊鵲尾、江城，皆有功。

translations.literal: He also struck Magpie Tail and River City, winning merit in each.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Magpie Tail and River City as well, and won credit in both.

sentences.zh: 事平，明帝大會新亭，勞接諸軍主，樗蒲官賭，安民五擲皆盧，帝大驚，目安民曰：「卿面方如田，封侯狀也。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Mingdi held a great gathering at Xinting to reward the army commanders; the court set up otree for official gambling. Anmin cast five times and each throw came up blank; the emperor was greatly startled and fixed his eyes on Anmin, saying: 「Your face is square as a field—the bearing of one who will be enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: After peace returned, Mingdi feasted the commanders at Xinting and set out otree dice for court gambling. Anmin threw five times and every cast came up blank; the emperor started in wonder and stared at him. 「Your face is broad as a plowed field,」 he said. 「That is the look of a man born to be made a lord.

sentences.zh: 」安民少時貧窶，有一人從門過，相之曰：「君后當大富貴，與天子交手共戲。

translations.literal: 」When Anmin was young he was destitute; a man passing the door read his face and said: 「You will later be vastly rich and noble and will play hand to hand with the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 」In his youth Anmin had been poor; once a stranger walking past the gate studied his face and said: 「You are destined for great wealth and rank—you will sport with the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 」至是安民尋此人，不知所在。

translations.literal: 」By then Anmin searched for this man but could not find where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: 」Now Anmin tried to find him again, but the man had vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 從張永、沈攸之討薛安都於彭城，軍敗，安民在后拒戰，還保下邳。

translations.literal: He followed Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi in the campaign against Xue Andu at Pengcheng; the army was beaten, but Anmin held the rear and fought, then fell back to defend Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi against Xue Andu at Pengcheng; when the army broke, Anmin fought a rearguard action and withdrew to hold Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 除寧朔將軍，戍淮陽城。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the North and garrisoned Huaiyang city.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General Who Pacifies the North and posted to the walls of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 論<魚貴>口功，封邵武縣子，食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: On his merit at the Yugui crossing he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shaowu, with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his victory at the Yugui ford he was made Viscount of Shaowu, with four hundred households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 復隨吳喜、沈攸之擊虜，達睢口，戰敗，還保宿豫。

translations.literal: He again followed Wu Xi and Shen Youzhi in striking the barbarians, reached Sui Ford, was defeated, and fell back to hold Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again with Wu Xi and Shen Youzhi against the northerners, pushed to Sui Ford, was thrown back, and retreated to defend Suyu.

sentences.zh: 淮北旣沒，明帝敕留安民戍角城。

translations.literal: Once the north bank of the Huai had fallen, Mingdi ordered Anmin to remain and garrison Jiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai north shore was lost, Mingdi commanded Anmin to stay and hold Jiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 除寧朔將軍、冗從僕射。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the North and supernumerary attendant-within-the-gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the rank of General Who Pacifies the North and supernumerary attendant-within-the-gates.

sentences.zh: 戍泗口，領舟軍緣淮游防，至壽春。

translations.literal: He garrisoned the Sizhou ford, led the boat army patrolling along the Huai, and reached Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He held the ford at Sizhou, commanded the river fleet on patrol along the Huai, and advanced as far as Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 虜遣偽長社公連營十餘里寇汝陰，豫州刺史劉勔擊退之。

translations.literal: The barbarians sent the false Changshe Duke with linked camps stretching more than ten li to raid Yuyin; Liu Mian, inspector of Yu, drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent the puppet Changshe Duke with a chain of camps more than ten li long against Yuyin; Liu Mian, inspector of Yu, beat them back.

sentences.zh: 虜荊亭戍主昇乞奴棄城歸降，安民率水軍攻前，破荊亭，絕其津逕。

translations.literal: The barbarian garrison chief of Jingting, Sheng Qinu, abandoned the city and came over; Anmin led the naval forces in the van, broke Jingting, and cut their crossings and roads.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Qinu, the northern garrison chief at Jingting, deserted and surrendered; Anmin drove the fleet ahead, stormed Jingting, and severed every ford and path behind them.

sentences.zh: 遷寧朔將軍、冠軍司馬、廣陵太守、行南兖州事。

translations.literal: He was moved to General Who Pacifies the North, champion chief clerk, administrator of Guangling, and acting overseer of southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North, made champion chief clerk and administrator of Guangling, and put in charge of southern Yanzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 太祖在淮陰，安民遙相結事，明帝以為疑，徙安民為劉韞冠軍司馬、寧朔將軍、京兆太守，又除寧朔將軍、司州刺史，領義陽太守，竝不拜，重除本職，又不拜，改授寧朔將軍、山陽太守。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor was then at Huaiyin; Anmin allied himself with him from afar. Mingdi grew suspicious and transferred Anmin to be champion chief clerk to Liu Yun, General Who Pacifies the North, and administrator of Jingzhao; he was again made General Who Pacifies the North, inspector of Si, and leading administrator of Yiyang—posts he refused. He was reappointed to his former duties and again would not accept; he was then changed to General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor stood at Huaiyin, and Anmin bound himself to him from a distance. Mingdi took alarm and shifted him to Liu Yun's champion chief clerk, with the same general's rank and the governorship of Jingzhao; then to General Who Pacifies the North, inspector of Si, and governor of Yiyang—all declined. The court restored his old posts; he declined again. At last he was named General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 泰始末，淮北民起義欲南歸，以安民督前鋒軍事，又請援接，不克，還。

translations.literal: At the end of Taishi the people north of the Huai rose to return south; Anmin was put in overall command of the vanguard, asked for reinforcements and support, failed, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Taishi the Huai north rose to come south again; Anmin was made overseer of the vanguard, begged for relief that never came, and marched back empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 除越騎校尉，復為寧朔將軍、山陽太守。

translations.literal: He was made Colonel of Rapid Cavalry and again General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Colonel of Rapid Cavalry, then once more General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 三巴擾亂，太守張澹棄涪城走，以安民假節、都督討蜀軍事、輔師將軍。

translations.literal: The Three Ba were in turmoil; the administrator Zhang Tan abandoned Fucheng and fled. Anmin was given the tally, made overall commander of the campaign against Shu, and appointed General Who Assists the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Ba erupted, Governor Zhang Tan deserted Fucheng and ran. Anmin received the tally, was made overall commander of the Shu expedition, and took the rank of General Who Assists the Army.

sentences.zh: 五獠亂漢中，敕安民回軍至魏興，事寧，還至夏口。

translations.literal: The Five Liao troubled Hanzhong; the emperor ordered Anmin to wheel his army back to Weixing. When the trouble ended he returned to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Five Liao bands ravaged Hanzhong; the throne ordered Anmin to swing his troops to Weixing. When order returned he came back to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，除督司州軍事、司州刺史，領義陽太守，假節、將軍如故。

translations.literal: At the opening of Yuanhui he was made overall commander of Si military affairs, inspector of Si, and leading administrator of Yiyang; his tally and general's rank were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first days of Yuanhui he was named overall commander of Si, inspector of the province, and governor of Yiyang, with tally and general's rank as before.

sentences.zh: 別敕安民曰：「九江須防，邊備宜重，今有此授，以增鄢郢之勢，無所致辭也。

translations.literal: A separate edict to Anmin said: 「Jiujiang must be guarded and the frontier prepared with weight; this appointment is given to strengthen the power of Yan and Ying—you are not to decline it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him a private command: 「Jiujiang must be watched, and the border girded with care. This post is meant to stiffen the defenses of Yan and Ying—do not refuse it.

sentences.zh: 」及桂陽王休範范起事，安民出頓，遣軍援京師。

translations.literal: 」When the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan, rose in rebellion, Anmin went out to encamp and sent troops to aid the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 」When Prince Xiu Fan of Guiyang rebelled, Anmin moved out to take the field and dispatched troops to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 徵［授］左將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left General and added as attendant-within-the-gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Left General and given the added post of attendant-within-the-gates.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素作難，冠軍黃回、游擊將軍高道慶、輔國將軍曹欣之等皆密遣致誠，而游擊將軍高道慶領衆出討，太祖慮其有變，使安民及南豫州刺史段佛榮行以防之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jianping, Jingsu, made trouble, the champion Huang Hui, Mobile Strike General Gao Daoqing, and Assists-the-State General Cao Xinzhi all secretly sent him pledges of loyalty; yet Mobile Strike General Gao Daoqing was ordered to lead troops out against him. The Grand Ancestor feared a turn of coat and sent Anmin and Duan Forong, inspector of southern Yuzhou, on patrol to guard against it.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jingsu of Jianping rose, Huang Hui the champion, Gao Daoqing the mobile-strike general, and Cao Xinzhi who assists the state all secretly offered him their faith—while Gao Daoqing was still ordered to march against him. The Grand Ancestor dreaded treachery and sent Anmin and Duan Forong of southern Yuzhou to shadow the columns.

sentences.zh: 安民至京［口］，破景素軍於葛橋。

translations.literal: Anmin reached Jingkou and broke Jingsu's army at Ge Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin came to Jingkou and shattered Jingsu's force at Ge Bridge.

sentences.zh: 景素誅，留安民行南徐州事。

translations.literal: After Jingsu was executed, Anmin was retained to administer southern Xuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingsu had been put to death, Anmin was left in charge of southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 城局參軍王迥素為安民所親，盜絹二匹，安民流涕謂之曰：「我與卿契闊備嘗，今日犯王法，此乃卿負我也。

translations.literal: The city-bureau staff officer Wang Jiong had long been close to Anmin; he stole two bolts of silk. Anmin, weeping, told him: 「You and I have shared hardship through thick and thin; today you have broken the king's law—this is you failing me.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiong of the city bureau had been his intimate; he stole two bolts of silk. Anmin said to him through tears: 「We have stood together through every trial; now you have broken the law of the land—that is you turning your back on me.

sentences.zh: 」於軍門斬之，厚為斂祭，軍府皆震服。

translations.literal: 」He had him beheaded at the army gate, gave him a lavish burial and rites of mourning, and the whole headquarters submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: 」He struck off his head before the camp gate, then buried him with full honor; every office in the command trembled into obedience.

sentences.zh: 授冠軍將軍，驍衛將軍，不拜。

translations.literal: He was granted the ranks of champion general and valiant guard general but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: They offered him champion general and valiant guard general; he would not take either.

sentences.zh: 轉征虜將軍、東中郎司馬、行會稽郡事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Subdues the Barbarians, chief clerk of the Eastern Central Commandant, and acting administrator of Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to General Who Subdues the Barbarians, made chief clerk to the Eastern Central Commandant, and set over Kuaiji commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 安民將東，太祖與別宴語，淹留日夜。

translations.literal: As Anmin was about to go east, the Grand Ancestor held a parting banquet and talked with him, keeping him through the day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When Anmin was ready to sail east, the Grand Ancestor gave him a farewell feast and kept him talking from dusk to dawn.

sentences.zh: 安民密陳宋運將盡，歷數有歸。

translations.literal: Anmin secretly reported that Song's fortune was nearing its end and the mandate of succession had found its home.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin secretly told the Grand Ancestor that Song's luck was spent and Heaven's count had already chosen its lord.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧縱虐，太祖憂迫無計，安民白太祖欲於東奉江夏王躋起兵，太祖不許，乃止。

translations.literal: Cangwu ran wild with cruelty; the Grand Ancestor was pressed with worry and had no plan. Anmin told the Grand Ancestor he wished to rise in the east supporting the Prince of Jiangxia Ji; the Grand Ancestor did not consent, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Cangwu's cruelty ran unchecked, and the Grand Ancestor was cornered without a plan. Anmin urged him to raise arms in the east behind Prince Jiangxia Ji; the Grand Ancestor refused, and the scheme died.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧廢，太祖徵安民為使持節督北討軍事、冠軍將軍、南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: When Cangwu was deposed, the Grand Ancestor summoned Anmin as commissioner with full powers directing the northern punitive campaign, champion general, and inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cangwu was cast down, the Grand Ancestor called Anmin in as commissioner with full powers over the northern punitive campaign, champion general, and inspector of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之反，太祖召安民以本官鎮白下，治城隍，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, the Grand Ancestor recalled Anmin in his existing rank to hold Baixia, repair walls and moats, and added the title general who captures the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi turned rebel, the Grand Ancestor recalled Anmin in his present rank to hold Baixia, raise walls and moats, and made him general who captures the enemy as well.

sentences.zh: 進軍西討，又進前將軍。

translations.literal: He advanced west on campaign and was further promoted to forward general.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west to punish the rebels and was further raised to forward general.

sentences.zh: 行至盆城，沈攸之平，仍授督郢州司州之義陽諸軍事、郢州刺史，持節、將軍如故。

translations.literal: Reaching Pencheng, when Shen Youzhi was pacified, he was then given command of all military affairs in Yingzhou and Yiyang in Sizhou, made inspector of Yingzhou, with staff and general as before.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Pencheng as Youzhi fell; he was then made overall commander of Yingzhou and of Yiyang in Sizhou, inspector of Yingzhou, with staff and general unchanged.

sentences.zh: 昇明三年，遷左衛將軍，領衛尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming he was moved to left guard general and also headed the guard commandant's office.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 3 he was shifted to left guard general and also took charge of the guard commandant's office.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，為中領軍，封康樂侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor took the throne, Anmin was made director of the central army and enfeoffed as Marquis of Kangle with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor acceded, Anmin became director of the central army and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Kangle with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始以來，內外頻有賊寇，將帥已下，各募部曲，屯聚京師。

translations.literal: Since Song's Taishi era, bandits had struck again and again within and without; commanders and below each raised private followings and gathered them in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song's Taishi reign, raids had come one after another inside the realm and along the borders; every commander down the ranks raised his own following and crowded them into the capital.

sentences.zh: 安民上表陳之，以為：「自非淮北常備，其外餘軍，悉皆輸遣。

translations.literal: Anmin memorialized on it, saying: 「Except for the standing garrisons on the Huai north, all other troops should be sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin submitted a memorial, arguing: 「Save the standing garrisons north of the Huai; every other force should be marched out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 若親近宜立隨身者，聽限人數。

translations.literal: If close attendants need a personal escort, let the numbers be limited.」
translations.idiomatic: Where a man truly needs a household guard, set a fixed head count.」

sentences.zh: 」上納之，故詔斷衆募。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it, and therefore issued an edict cutting off mass recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: The throne took the advice and issued an edict forbidding private levies.

sentences.zh: 時王敬則以勳誠見親，至於家國密事，上唯與安民論議，謂安民曰：「署事有卿名，我便不復細覽也。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jingze was held close for his meritorious loyalty; on state and family secrets the emperor discussed only with Anmin, saying to him: 「When documents bear your name, I no longer read them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze then stood among the emperor's trusted men of merit; on the gravest affairs of house and realm the throne spoke only with Anmin and told him, 「If your name is on the docket, I will not pore over it myself.

sentences.zh: 」尋為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: 」Soon after he was made director of the army.
translations.idiomatic: 」Before long he was made director of the army.

sentences.zh: 虜寇壽春，至馬頭。

translations.literal: The barbarians raided Shouchun and reached Matou.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians struck Shouchun and pushed as far as Matou.

sentences.zh: 詔安民出征，加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Anmin on campaign and added one set of drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Anmin to the field and granted him one suite of martial music.

sentences.zh: 虜退，安民沿淮進壽春。

translations.literal: The barbarians retreated; Anmin advanced along the Huai to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians drew back, Anmin moved up the Huai into Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 先是宋世亡命王元初聚黨六合山僣號，自云垂手過膝。

translations.literal: Earlier, a Song-era outlaw named Wang Yuanchu had gathered a band on Liuhe Mountain, taken a false title, and claimed his hands hung past his knees.
translations.idiomatic: Years before, a Song fugitive named Wang Yuanchu had raised a host on Liuhe Mountain, styled himself king, and boasted that his hands reached below his knees.

sentences.zh: 州部討不能擒，積十餘年。

translations.literal: The province and commanderies had attacked but could not capture him; more than ten years passed.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery troops had hunted him without success for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 安民遣軍偵候，生禽元初，斬建康市。

translations.literal: Anmin sent troops to scout; they took Yuanchu alive and beheaded him in the Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin sent scouts; they seized Yuanchu alive and beheaded him in the Jiankang market.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was given the added title attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered riders.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered riders.

sentences.zh: 其年，虜又南侵，詔安民持節履行緣淮清泗諸戍屯軍。

translations.literal: That year the barbarians invaded south again; an edict made Anmin commissioner with the staff to inspect all garrison troops along the Huai and the Qing-Si line.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the barbarians came south again; an edict sent Anmin out with the staff to review every garrison along the Huai and the Qing-Si frontier.

sentences.zh: 虜攻朐山、連口、角城，安民頓泗口，分軍應赴。

translations.literal: The barbarians attacked Qushan, Liankou, and Jiaocheng; Anmin halted at Sikou and divided his army to respond.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians hit Qushan, Liankou, and Jiaocheng; Anmin held Sikou and split his forces to answer each alarm.

sentences.zh: 三年，引水步軍入清，于淮陽與虜戰，破之。

translations.literal: In the third year he led infantry by water into the Qing, fought the barbarians at Huaiyang, and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he brought infantry by water into the Qing, met the barbarians at Huaiyang, and broke them.

sentences.zh: 虜退，安民知有伏兵，乃遣族弟馬軍主長文二百騎為前驅，自與軍副周盤龍、崔文仲係其後，分軍隱林。

translations.literal: The barbarians withdrew; Anmin knew there were ambush troops, so he sent his cousin the horse-army commander Changwen with two hundred horsemen as vanguard, himself with army aides Zhou Panlong and Cui Wenzhong following behind, and split forces hidden in the woods.
translations.idiomatic: As the barbarians pulled back, Anmin guessed at an ambush. He sent his cousin Changwen, horse-army commander, ahead with two hundred riders, followed with Zhou Panlong and Cui Wenzhong as his deputies, and hid the rest of the host in the woods.

sentences.zh: 及長文至宿豫，虜見衆少，數千騎遮之。

translations.literal: When Changwen reached Suyu, the barbarians saw his force was small and several thousand horsemen blocked him.
translations.idiomatic: At Suyu the barbarians saw how few men Changwen had and threw several thousand riders across his path.

sentences.zh: 長文且退且戰，引賊向大軍，安民率盤龍等趨兵至，合戰於孫溪渚戰父彎側，虜軍大敗，赴清水死不可勝數。

translations.literal: Changwen fought while retreating, drawing the enemy toward the main force; Anmin led Panlong and the rest at speed to the field; they joined battle beside Sunxi ford at Zhanfu bend; the barbarian army was utterly defeated; those who plunged into Qingshui and drowned were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Changwen gave ground fighting, baiting the enemy toward the main host; Anmin drove Panlong and the rest to the spot; at Sunxi ford, beside Zhanfu bend, the two sides crashed together and the barbarians were shattered—men drowned in Qingshui in numbers no one could count.

sentences.zh: 虜遣其菟頭公送攻車材至布丘，左軍將軍孫文顯擊破走之，燒其車材。

translations.literal: The barbarians sent their Tutou Gong delivering siege equipment to Buqiu; left army general Sun Wenxian struck, routed, and drove him off, and burned the siege materials.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians sent their Tutou Gong with siege timber to Buqiu; Sun Wenxian, left army general, broke him, drove him off, and burned the wagons.

sentences.zh: 淮北四州聞太祖受命，咸欲南歸。

translations.literal: The four Huai-north provinces heard the Grand Ancestor had received the mandate and all wished to return south.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that the Grand Ancestor had received Heaven's mandate, the four Huai-north provinces all yearned to come south.

sentences.zh: 至是徐州人桓摽之、兖州人徐猛子等，合義衆數萬，柴險求援。

translations.literal: At this time Huan Biaozhi of Xuzhou, Xu Mengzi of Yanzhou, and others combined righteous hosts of tens of thousands, fortified difficult ground, and begged for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Then Huan Biaozhi of Xuzhou, Xu Mengzi of Yanzhou, and others raised righteous bands by the tens of thousands, barred the passes, and cried for aid.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔曰：「青徐泗州，義舉雲集。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor's edict said: 「In Qing, Xu, and Si provinces the righteous risings gather like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor's edict read: 「In Qing, Xu, and Si the loyal rising gathers like a cloud.

sentences.zh: 安民可長轡遐馭，指授羣帥。

translations.literal: Anmin may take the long reins and drive from afar, directing all the commanders.」
translations.idiomatic: Let Anmin take the long reins and command from afar, setting every captain in its place.」

sentences.zh: 」安民赴救留遲，虜急兵攻摽之等皆沒，上甚責之。

translations.literal: Anmin went to the rescue but lingered; the barbarians' pressing troops attacked and Biaozhi and the rest were all destroyed; the emperor blamed him sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin marched to relieve them but came late; the barbarians' pressing columns swallowed Biaozhi and the rest; the throne rebuked him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，遺詔加侍中。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor died, his deathbed edict added palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the Grand Ancestor's death, the testamentary edict added palace attendant to his titles.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，遷撫軍將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Anmin was moved to general who pacifies the army and Danyang intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu acceded, Anmin was shifted to general who pacifies the army and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，遷尚書左僕射，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was moved to left vice director of the master of writing, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 2 he was made left vice director of the master of writing, his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 安民時屢啟密謀見賞，又善結尚書令王儉，故世傳儉啟有此授。

translations.literal: Anmin had repeatedly submitted secret stratagems and won praise; he was also skilled at cultivating Director of the Master of Writing Wang Jian, and so the world said Jian's memorial was why he received this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin had won favor again and again for secret counsel, and he knew how to court Wang Jian, director of the master of writing; people therefore said the post came from Jian's memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋上表以年疾求退，改授散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that age and illness made him wish to retire; he was reassigned as attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered riders and household minister with golden seal and purple ribbon, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked leave on grounds of age and illness; he was reassigned attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered riders and household minister with golden seal and purple ribbon, his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 四年，為安東將軍、吳興太守，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made general who pacifies the east and administrator of Wuxing, attendant-in-ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he became general who pacifies the east and administrator of Wuxing, still attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died in office at fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 賻錢十萬，布百匹。

translations.literal: Burial gift of one hundred thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted one hundred thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 吳興有項羽神護郡聽事，太守不得上。

translations.literal: In Wuxing there was a spirit of Xiang Yu guarding the prefectural audience hall; the administrator could not ascend it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing held a shrine to the spirit of Xiang Yu that guarded the prefectural hall; no administrator was said to climb its steps in peace.

sentences.zh: 太守到郡，必須祀以軛下牛。

translations.literal: When an administrator came to the commandery, he had to sacrifice an ox from beneath the yoke.
translations.idiomatic: Every new administrator had to offer an ox taken from beneath the yoke.

sentences.zh: 安民奉佛法，不與神牛，著屐上聽事。

translations.literal: Anmin followed the Buddhist dharma, would not provide the spirit's ox, and went up to the audience hall in wooden clogs.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin was a Buddhist; he refused the ox and climbed the hall in wooden clogs.

sentences.zh: 又於聽上設八關齋。

translations.literal: He also set up an eight-gate fast on the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall itself he held an eight-gate observance.

sentences.zh: 俄而牛死，葬廟側，今呼為「李公牛冢」。

translations.literal: Before long the ox died and was buried beside the temple; people now call it the 「Lord Li's Ox Tomb.」
translations.idiomatic: Soon the ox died and was buried beside the shrine; locals still call the mound 「Lord Li's Ox Tomb.」

sentences.zh: 及安民卒，世以神為祟。

translations.literal: When Anmin died, the world took it as the spirit's vengeance.
translations.idiomatic: When Anmin died, people said the spirit had taken its due.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「安民歷位內外，庸績顯著。

translations.literal: An edict said: 「Anmin served inside and outside the court; his solid achievements stood out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: 「Anmin held office at court and in the provinces; his steady service stood plain.

sentences.zh: 忠亮之誠，每簡朕心。

translations.literal: His loyal, bright sincerity ever pleased Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: His loyal, open heart ever won Our trust.

sentences.zh: 敷政近畿，方申任寄。

translations.literal: Governing the capital region, he had only begun to fulfill Our trust.
translations.idiomatic: He had only begun to carry Our charge in the capital lands.

sentences.zh: 奄至殞喪，痛傷于懷。

translations.literal: When he suddenly passed away, grief pierced the heart.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that he had died so soon, the throne was stricken with grief.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮東將軍，鼓吹一部，常侍、太守如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Guards the East, with one suite of martial music; attendant cavalier and administrator remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was named general who guards the east, with one suite of martial music; attendant cavalier and prefect stayed on the record.

sentences.zh: 諡曰肅侯。」

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Solemn.」
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Marquis Solemn.」

sentences.zh: 王玄載，字彥休，下邳人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanzai, styled Yanxiu, was a native of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanzai, styled Yanxiu, came from Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 祖宰，偽北地太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zai had been administrator of the Northern Region under the puppet regime.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zai had held the Northern Region under the puppet court.

sentences.zh: 父蕤，東莞太守。

translations.literal: His father Rui was administrator of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rui was administrator of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 玄載解褐江夏王國侍郎、太宰行參軍。

translations.literal: Xuanzai left the russet and became gentleman in the Prince of Jiangxia's establishment and acting staff officer on the grand commanderate.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzai first took office as gentleman in the Prince of Jiangxia's house and acting staff officer on the grand commanderate.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，為長水校尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was made colonel of the long river.
translations.idiomatic: When Taishi opened he was made colonel of the long river.

sentences.zh: 隨張永征彭城，臺軍大敗，玄載全軍據下邳城拒虜，假冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Zhang Yong against Pengcheng; the court army was routed, yet Xuanzai brought his whole force intact to hold Xiapi against the enemy and was given acting rank as champion.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Zhang Yong on Pengcheng; when the court army was shattered, Xuanzai kept his command whole, seized Xiapi, and held the northerners at bay—receiving acting rank as champion.

sentences.zh: 官軍新敗，人情恐駭，以玄載士望，板為徐州刺史、持節、監徐州豫州梁郡軍事、寧朔將軍、平胡中郎將，尋又領山陽、東海二郡太守。

translations.literal: The court army had just been beaten and hearts were terrified; because of Xuanzai's standing among the gentry he was commissioned inspector of Xuzhou, bearer of the tally, superintendent of military affairs in Xuzhou, Yuzhou, and Liang commandery, general who calms the north, and central commander who pacifies the Hu; soon he also held the administratorships of Shanyang and Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from defeat, the army quaked; on Xuanzai's gentry renown the court commissioned him inspector of Xu, bearer of the tally, superintendent of Xu, Yu, and Liang commandery, general who calms the north, and central commander who pacifies the Hu—then added Shanyang and Donghai as his prefectures.

sentences.zh: 五年，督青、兖二州刺史，將軍、東海郡如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he supervised Qing and Yan; his general's rank and Donghai commandery stayed as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he supervised Qing and Yan; his general's style and Donghai commandery were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 七年，復為徐州，督徐兖二州、鍾離太守，將軍、郎將如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he again took Xuzhou, supervising Xu and Yan and holding Zhongli as administrator; general and commandant ranks were as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he returned to Xu, supervising Xu and Yan and governing Zhongli; his general's and commandant's ranks stood as before.

sentences.zh: 遷左軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to general of the left army.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to general of the left army.

sentences.zh: 仍為寧朔將軍、歷陽太守，改持節、都督二豫、冠軍將軍、南豫州刺史，太守如故。

translations.literal: He remained general who calms the north and administrator of Liyang, then bore the staff as commander of the two Yus, champion general, and inspector of southern Yu, with the administratorship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Still general who calms the north and prefect of Liyang, he next bore the staff as commander of the two Yus, champion general, and inspector of southern Yu, keeping the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷撫軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was moved to major of the pacification army.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to major of the pacification army.

sentences.zh: 出為持節、督梁南北秦三州軍事、冠軍將軍、西戎校尉、梁秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out bearing the staff as commander of military affairs in Liang, northern Qin, and southern Qin, champion general, western-barbarian commandant, and inspector of Liang and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He went out bearing the staff as commander of Liang, northern Qin, and southern Qin, champion general, western-barbarian commandant, and inspector of Liang and Qin.

sentences.zh: 進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to general who campaigns against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: His style rose to general who campaigns against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 尋徙督益寧二州、益州刺史、建寧太守，將軍、持節如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to supervise Yi and Ning, made inspector of Yi and administrator of Jianning, with general's rank and bearer of the staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he supervised Yi and Ning, took Yi as inspector and Jianning as prefect, and kept his general's rank and staff unchanged.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之之難，玄載起義送誠，進號后軍將軍，封鄂縣子。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Xuanzai rose in loyal arms and pledged his faith; his title was advanced to rear-army general and he was enfeoffed as viscount of E county.
translations.idiomatic: At Shen Youzhi's revolt Xuanzai raised loyal arms and sent his pledge; his rank rose to rear-army general and he was made viscount of E county.

sentences.zh: 征散騎常侍，領后軍，未拜，建元元年，為左民尚書，鄂縣子如故。

translations.literal: He was summoned as attendant cavalier of the scattered riders and was to hold the rear army, but did not accept the appointment; in the first year of Jianyuan he became household minister for the people, viscount of E as before.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him as attendant cavalier of the scattered riders to lead the rear army, but he never took the seal; in Jianyuan year one he became household minister for the people, still viscount of E.

sentences.zh: 會虜動，南兖州刺史王敬則奔京師，上遣玄載領廣陵，加平北將軍、假節、行南兖州事，本官如故。

translations.literal: When the barbarians stirred, southern Yan inspector Wang Jingze fled to the capital; the emperor sent Xuanzai to take Guangling, added general who pacifies the north, acting tally, and charge of southern Yan affairs, with his former offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the northerners moved, Wang Jingze, inspector of southern Yan, fled to the capital; the throne sent Xuanzai to hold Guangling, added general who pacifies the north, an acting tally, and charge of southern Yan—his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 事寧，為光祿大夫、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he became grand master of splendid happiness and supernumerary attendant cavalier of the scattered riders.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace returned he was grand master of splendid happiness and supernumerary attendant cavalier of the scattered riders.

sentences.zh: 永明四年，為持節監兖州緣淮諸軍事、平北將軍、兖州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming he bore the staff as superintendent of all military affairs along the Huai frontier in Yan, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year four he bore the staff as superintendent of all Huai-frontier forces in Yan, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he died, at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 諡烈子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Viscount Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Viscount Fierce.

sentences.zh: 玄載夷雅好玄言，脩士操，在梁益有清績，西州至今思之。

translations.literal: Xuanzai was refined and fond of arcane discourse; he cultivated gentlemanly conduct. In Liang and Yi he won a clear record, and the western provinces remember him still.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzai was grave and elegant, drawn to arcane talk, and strict in gentleman's conduct; in Liang and Yi his rule was clean, and the west still speaks his name.

sentences.zh: 玄載弟玄邈，字彥遠。

translations.literal: Xuanzai's younger brother Xuanmiao was styled Yanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzai's younger brother Xuanmiao, styled Yanyuan.

sentences.zh: 初為驃騎行軍參軍，太子左積弩將軍，射聲校尉。

translations.literal: At first he was army staff officer on the rapid-cavalry staff, left accumulative-crossbow general to the crown prince, and colonel of the sounding archers.
translations.idiomatic: He began as army staff officer on the rapid-cavalry staff, left accumulative-crossbow general to the crown prince, and colonel of the sounding archers.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，遷輔國將軍、清河廣川二郡太守，幽州刺史。
