translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was moved to general who assists the state, administrator of Qinghe and Guangchuan, and inspector of You.
translations.idiomatic: When Taishi opened he became general who assists the state, prefect of Qinghe and Guangchuan, and inspector of You.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史沈文秀反，玄邈欲向朝廷，慮見掩襲，乃詣文秀求安軍頓。

translations.literal: When Yan inspector Shen Wenxiu rebelled, Xuanmiao wished to join the court but feared being overrun, so he went to Wenxiu and asked leave to encamp in safety.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Wenxiu, inspector of Yan, rebelled, Xuanmiao meant to march for the throne but feared a sudden strike; he went to Wenxiu and asked for a safe camp.

sentences.zh: 文秀令頓城外。

translations.literal: Wenxiu ordered him to halt outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu made him camp outside the city.

sentences.zh: 玄邈卽立營壘，至夜拔軍南奔赴義。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao at once threw up ramparts; by night he broke camp and marched south to join the loyal cause.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao threw up earthworks at once; that night he broke camp and ran south to the loyal standard.

sentences.zh: 比曉，文秀追不復及。

translations.literal: By dawn Wenxiu's pursuit could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn Wenxiu's pursuers could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 明帝以為持節、都督青州、青州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming made him bearer of the staff, commander of Qing, and inspector of Qing, with his general's rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming named him bearer of the staff, commander of Qing, and inspector of Qing, his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮淮陰，為帝所疑，遣書結玄邈。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor was garrisoned at Huaiyin and fell under the emperor's suspicion; he sent letters to win Xuanmiao over.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor held Huaiyin, came under imperial suspicion, and sent letters to bind Xuanmiao to him.

sentences.zh: 玄邈長史房叔安勸玄邈不相答和。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao's chief clerk Fang Shuan urged him not to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Fang Shuan urged Xuanmiao to send no reply.

sentences.zh: 罷州還，太祖以經途令人要之，玄邈雖許，旣而嚴軍直過，還都啟帝，稱太祖有異謀，太祖不恨也。

translations.literal: When he left his province and returned, the Grand Ancestor sent men to intercept him on the road; Xuanmiao agreed, yet tightened his troops and passed straight through, and on reaching the capital reported to the emperor that the Grand Ancestor harbored treacherous designs—the Grand Ancestor bore no grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving office, he passed the Grand Ancestor's route; the Grand Ancestor sent men to waylay him. Xuanmiao assented on paper, then closed ranks and marched through; back in the capital he told the emperor the Grand Ancestor nursed treason—and the Grand Ancestor did not resent it.

sentences.zh: 昇明中，太祖引為驃騎司馬、冠軍將軍、太山太守，玄邈甚懼，而太祖待之如初。

translations.literal: In the Shengming years the Grand Ancestor drew him in as rapid-cavalry major, champion general, and administrator of Taishan; Xuanmiao was greatly afraid, yet the Grand Ancestor treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengming years the Grand Ancestor took him as rapid-cavalry major, champion general, and prefect of Taishan; Xuanmiao was terrified, but the Grand Ancestor received him as ever.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、驍騎將軍，冠軍如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to attendant cavalier of the scattered riders and general of raiding cavalry, champion as before.
translations.idiomatic: He became attendant cavalier of the scattered riders and general of raiding cavalry, still champion.

sentences.zh: 還為征虜將軍、長沙王後軍司馬、南東海太守。

translations.literal: He returned as general who campaigns against the enemy, rear-army major to the Prince of Changsha, and administrator of southern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as general who campaigns against the enemy, rear-army major to the Prince of Changsha, and prefect of southern Donghai.

sentences.zh: 遷都官尚書。

translations.literal: He was moved to minister of the court offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to minister of the court offices.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，轉右將軍、豫章王太尉司馬，出為冠軍將軍、臨川內史，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne he became right general and grand-commandant major to the Prince of Yuzhang; he went out as champion general and interior minister of Linchuan at the salary of middle two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu ascended he was right general and grand-commandant major to the Prince of Yuzhang, then went out as champion general and interior minister of Linchuan at middle two-thousand-shi pay.

sentences.zh: 還為前軍司徒司馬、散騎常侍、太子右率。

translations.literal: He returned as van-army grand-mentor major, attendant cavalier of the scattered riders, and right commander of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He came back as van-army grand-mentor major, attendant cavalier of the scattered riders, and right commander of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 永明七年，為持節、都督兖州緣淮軍事、平北將軍、兖州刺史，未之任，轉大司馬，加后將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming he bore the staff as commander of Yan's Huai-frontier military affairs, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of Yan; he did not take up the post and was moved to grand marshal with added rank as rear-army general.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year seven he bore the staff as commander of Yan's Huai-frontier forces, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of Yan—yet never took the post, and was made grand marshal with added rank as rear-army general.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉太常，遷散騎常侍、右衛將軍，出為持節、監徐州軍事、平北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to grand master of ceremonies, then made attendant cavalier of the scattered riders and general of the right guard; he went out bearing the staff as superintendent of Xuzhou military affairs, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he became grand master of ceremonies, then attendant cavalier of the scattered riders and general of the right guard; he went out bearing the staff as superintendent of Xu, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，建康蓮華寺道人釋法智與州民周盤龍等作亂，四百人夜攻州城西門，登梯上城，射殺城局參軍唐潁，遂入城內。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the monk Shifazhi of Lianhua Temple in Jiankang and Zhou Panlong of the province and others rebelled; four hundred men by night attacked the western gate of the provincial city, climbed ladders onto the wall, shot and killed rampart-bureau staff officer Tang Ying, and entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven the monk Shifazhi of Jiankang's Lianhua Temple and Zhou Panlong of the province rose with others; four hundred men struck the western gate by night, scaled the wall on ladders, shot down rampart officer Tang Ying, and broke into the city.

sentences.zh: 軍主耿虎、徐思慶、董文定等拒戰，至曉，玄邈率百餘人登城便門，奮擊，生擒法智、盤龍等。

translations.literal: Army commanders Geng Hu, Xu Siqing, Dong Wending, and others fought them off; by dawn Xuanmiao led a little over a hundred men up the convenient gate of the wall, struck hard, and took Fazhi, Panlong, and the rest alive.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Geng Hu, Xu Siqing, Dong Wending, and the rest held them through the night; at dawn Xuanmiao climbed the postern with a little over a hundred men, struck hard, and took Fazhi, Panlong, and their fellows alive.

sentences.zh: 玄邈坐免官。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao was stripped of office on account of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao was dismissed from office over the affair.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，授撫軍將軍，遷使持節、安西將軍、歷陽南譙二郡太守。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne he was made general of the pacification army, then bearer of constant staff, general who pacifies the west, and administrator of Liyang and Nanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin ascended he was named general of the pacification army, then bearer of constant staff, general who pacifies the west, and prefect of Liyang and Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，加散騎常侍，尋轉中護軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was added as attendant cavalier of the scattered riders; soon he was moved to central protector of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing year one he gained attendant cavalier of the scattered riders; soon he was made central protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 同族王文和，宋鎮北大將軍仲德兄孫也。

translations.literal: A clansman, Wang Wenhe, was a grandson of the elder brother of Song's general who guards the north, Zhongde.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman, Wang Wenhe, was grandson of the elder brother of Song's northern guardian general Wang Zhongde.

sentences.zh: 景和中，為義陽王昶征北府主簿。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era he served as registrar of the northern expedition staff of Prince Chang of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe years he was registrar on Prince Chang of Yiyang's northern expedition staff.

sentences.zh: 昶于彭城奔虜，部曲皆散，文和獨送至界上。

translations.literal: When Chang fled to the northerners at Pengcheng, his retainers all scattered; Wenhe alone escorted him to the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang bolted to the northerners at Pengcheng, his following melted away; Wenhe alone saw him to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 昶謂之曰：「諸人皆去，卿有老母，何不去邪！

translations.literal: Chang said to him: 「All the others have gone; you have an aged mother—why do you not leave as well!
translations.idiomatic: Chang told him: 「Everyone else has gone; you still have an old mother at home—why not leave too!

sentences.zh: 」文和乃去。

translations.literal: 」Wenhe then departed.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wenhe withdrew.

sentences.zh: 昇明中，為巴陵內史。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era he was made interior secretary of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengming years he became interior secretary of Baling.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，文和斬其使，馳白世祖告變，棄郡奔郢城。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair broke out, Wenhe beheaded his envoy, galloped to report the treason to Shizu, abandoned the commandery, and fled to Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rose in rebellion, Wenhe cut down his messenger, raced to Shizu with word of the plot, left his prefecture, and ran to Ying.

sentences.zh: 永明中，歷青、冀、兖、益四州刺史，平北將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he successively held the four inspectorates of Qing, Ji, Yan, and Yi, and was made general who pacifies the north.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongming he served in turn as inspector of Qing, Ji, Yan, and Yi, and as general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：宋氏將季，離亂日兆，家懷逐鹿，人有異圖。

translations.literal: The historian writes: The Song house was nearing its end; the signs of division and chaos grew daily; every family harbored the thought of seizing the deer, and every man nursed a separate design.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Song's fortune was spent; disorder gathered day by day; households dreamed of seizing the realm, and men each nursed schemes of their own.

sentences.zh: 故蕃岳阻兵之機，州郡觀釁之會。

translations.literal: Therefore frontier lords seized the moment to block arms, and provinces and commanderies watched for a chance to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier princes therefore readied arms, and provinces and commanderies watched for the opening blow.

sentences.zh: 此數子皆宿將舊勛，與太祖比肩為方伯，年位高下，或為先輩，而薦誠君側，奉義萬里。

translations.literal: These several men were all veteran generals of old merit; they stood shoulder to shoulder with the Grand Ancestor as regional lords; in age and rank some were his seniors, yet they offered loyalty at the sovereign's side and bore righteousness a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: These men were seasoned commanders of long service; they had stood as regional peers beside the Grand Ancestor, and in years or rank some were his elders—yet they pledged loyalty at the throne and carried the cause a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 以此知樂推之非妄，信民心之有歸。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the people's willing elevation was no empty tale, and may trust that hearts had found their home.
translations.idiomatic: Hence one sees that the people's willing push to the throne was no vain rumor, and that the realm's hearts had truly chosen their lord.

sentences.zh: 玄載兄弟門從，世秉誠烈，不為道家所忌，斯今之耿氏也。

translations.literal: Xuanzai and his brothers and cousins, generation after generation, held to sincere valor; not hated by the Daoist faction—they are the Geng clan of our day.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzai's brothers and cousins, line after line, kept to loyal ardor; untouched by the Daoist faction's spite—they are today's house of Geng.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：霄城報馬，分義先推。

translations.literal: In praise: Xiaocheng repays the horse; shared righteousness pushed first.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Xiaocheng returns the horse; shared duty led the way.

sentences.zh: 靈哲守讓，方軌丁、韋。

translations.literal: Ling Zhe keeps yielding; he matches the track of Ding and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Zhe holds to yielding; he walks the same path as Ding and Wei.

sentences.zh: 李佐東土，謀發天機。

translations.literal: Li assists the eastern lands; counsel stirs Heaven's design.
translations.idiomatic: Li steadies the eastern marches; stratagem moves Heaven's plan.

sentences.zh: 王為清政，其風不衰。

translations.literal: Wang governs with pure rule; that wind does not fade.
translations.idiomatic: Wang rules with clean government; that manner does not fail.

sentences.zh: 玄邈簡朕，早背同歸。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao austere and spare, early turned from the common road to return together.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao plain and restrained, early broke from the crowd to come home with the rest.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text has used as the base for collation the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi, January 1972.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi (January 1972).
